artifact.summary:
CHOSEN APPROACH: reuse an existing proven mechanism rather than invent one. functions/scripts/backfill-subscription-history.js (entity 051) already performs a safe bulk write against this exact sheet — deterministic ids, --analyze/--dry-run/--apply phases, batched all-or-nothing insertDimension+updateCells, skip-if-id-present idempotency, and PartialWriteError carrying already-written ids. This feature copies that shape; only the source parsing is new.

RISKIEST UNVERIFIED MECHANISM, AND WHAT EXERCISING IT SHOWED: reading the source workbook at all. Exercised, and it FAILED. Both Drive reads of file id 1PThKs3kePy294j5-0cK3ii1ZPAlkAkcgRdoE-6-o04I returned "Requested entity was not found"; a title search returned only work-account files, confirming the connector is authenticated to the wrong Google account. The Firebase service-account route was probed and rejected — the workbook was never shared with it. This is the one thing that must be resolved before build. Every other mechanism in the feature is already proven by the 051 precedent.

A SECOND, VERIFIED FINDING the checklist did not ask for: functions/scripts/load-local-env.js resolves SPREADSHEET_ID from functions/.env or the repo-root .env.local, and never from functions/.env.staging. An admin script therefore inherits a target rather than being given one, and cannot be aimed at staging at all today. AC-12 makes refusing to run without an explicit --target a shipped property, and D3-A exists because of this.

EXPECTED FILES AND LINES, WITH TOLERANCE: +700 net LOC across 4 files, tolerance +/-30%.
- functions/scripts/migrate-historical-expenses.js — new, ~450-600 LOC (parse, classify, plan, dry-run, apply, verify, undo)
- functions/test/migrate-historical-expenses.test.js — new, ~150 LOC against local JSON fixtures
- functions/scripts/load-local-env.js — ~15-25 LOC for --target staging|production
- functions/package.json — 4-6 script entries
Semantics changed: stored data only — new rows in the production Expenses tab, plus the Categories tab if D1-B or D1-D is chosen. No API shape change, no auth change, no scheduled-behavior change, no client change.

PROPOSED PROOF FOR EACH ACCEPTANCE CRITERION: 13 criteria, each carrying both a Verified by clause and the concrete Falsified by edit that would break it. Verification split is declared: OFFLINE for AC-1 through AC-6 and AC-9 through AC-13; INTERACTIVE for AC-7 and AC-8, judged on a live drive of the deployed app with no harness built to automate them.
- AC-1 no pre-existing row altered or deleted (snapshot/verify diff, 0 modified 0 deleted)
- AC-2 each year reconciles to the workbook total within 1% (verify prints computed, source, variance)
- AC-3 no aggregate or untagged row became an expense (dry-run classified count equals planned count)
- AC-4 income-side rows absent after import (verify asserts zero, lists excluded buckets)
- AC-5 re-running writes nothing (second apply reports created: 0)
- AC-6 undo restores the tab and touches nothing else (snapshot/apply/undo diff; a hand-added row survives)
- AC-7 Reports > Annual shows a non-zero total matching AC-2 within 1% (interactive live drive)
- AC-8 everyday use unaffected: add/see/delete an expense, History loads (interactive live drive)
- AC-9 every imported category_id resolves to a live category (verify asserts, reports Categories row count before/after)
- AC-10 every imported row records its origin (notes parse yields bucket, sub-category, row-kind, source year-month)
- AC-11 no figure, vendor, or account identifier committed to this public repo (git check-ignore plus full-diff read)
- AC-12 the import refuses to run without an explicit --target (exits non-zero, writes nothing)
- AC-13 whether 2023 has a record is settled by inspecting gid=0 and recorded before any write

CHECKLIST ACCOUNTING: 7 done, 0 skipped, 1 failed. The single failure is the gid=0 inspection, blocked on Drive account access, escalated rather than guessed, and carried structurally as decision D0 and as AC-13 which gates the import on that inspection.

AC EVIDENCE STATE: status --read 061 --stage spec --ac-scan now exits 0 and lists all 13 criteria; 10 report unevidenced, which is correct at spec — an AC earns its citation when the stage that proves it reports evidence, and nothing has been built yet.

selectors.exact: Does 2023 data actually exist? 060's recorded spec finding states the archive holds no 2023 record at all. The captain has since pointed at tab gid=0 of the 2024 workbook and asked to migrate "2024, 2023". Spec settles this by inspecting the tab, not by assuming either side is right. If 2023 genuinely has no record, this feature covers 2024 only and says so.

The app uses a flat gov_category set in app/app/lib/categories.ts. Spec decides what happens to buckets with no app equivalent, and whether the app's category set changes or the import approximates — this is a captain decision, not an implementer's.

annotations.body: we figure out the category first, we can leave gov_category later.

selectors.exact: Rental-property and income rows. The source tables interleave income rows and rental-property pass-through flows with household expense rows. Spec decides whether these are imported, excluded, or marked, since importing them silently distorts every total the app shows.

Aggregate rows are interleaved with data rows. Section totals and per-kind subtotals sit in the same columns as real line items; importing them double-counts. The row-kind tag in column A is the filter.
